key_insight: The paper shows that governing ODEs can be recovered from multiple solution trajectories by measuring equation distance on the induced solution sets, yielding identifiability and sample-complexity bounds for both linear and nonlinear systems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a theoretical foundation for scientific machine learning workflows that infer differential equations from data, helping engineers understand when learned dynamics are uniquely recoverable and how much trajectory data is needed.
method: Defines the Hausdorff distance between solution sets as the comparison metric for ODEs.
Derives identifiability bounds for linear ODEs and nonlinear ODEs with Lipschitz/Hölder continuous vector fields.
Uses metric entropy arguments to estimate sample complexity for recovering the governing equation from observations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and metric-entropy/sample-complexity bounds rather than a numerical benchmark, emphasizing provable recoverability conditions from solution data.
watch_item: The guarantees are mathematical and depend on the assumed ODE class and observation setting, so practical performance may be limited by noise, partial observability, or model mismatch.
paper_title: Recovering Governing Equations from Solution Data: Identifiability Bounds for Linear and Nonlinear ODEs
